---
title: "Association topology analysis"
subtitle: "Historical model-D association topology and transfer rules"
---

Historical association-topology decision for model D, the corrected-Born parameter formulation.

# Question

Which association topology and cross-association values were retained for historical model D in aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA), and were those values independently fitted?

# Result

Historical model D retained the two-site (2B) topology and induced CO₂–water association with energy [**1212.8500 K**]{.evidence-1}. These were declared or combining-rule inputs used in the bounded comparison, not independently fitted cross-association parameters. The retained choice does not establish topology uniqueness.

# Basis and method

The historical model-D record (the corrected-Born parameter formulation) (wheel `28181e72e429c6e87fc6361082af1a7b21c8747e76bda65a1c30abb4a97402f2`) is `9055458d8b7cd767a0d08e9f37e4fd28631e29c363364d7b842ebade645cb241`. Its packet-v5 topology uses the explicit Wolbach–Sandler MEA–water rule; historical values are tabulated below. The [adopted seventh-amendment (A7) record](../notebook.qmd#working-record) is separate.

[]{#starting-point}

The neutral components were represented with one donor and one acceptor site
(2B). The MEA choice follows the MEA association-scheme comparison in Baygi and
Pahlavanzadeh; the water and induced CO₂ choices follow the electrolyte perturbed-chain statistical associating fluid theory (ePC-SAFT) lineage
used for aqueous electrolyte mixtures. Association-scheme parameters are
conditional on the chosen scheme: changing 2B to three-site (3B) or four-site (4C) would require a new
pure-component parameterization, not a relabeling of the current numbers.

[]{#strategy}

The analysis keeps the topology fixed while checking whether the retained
cross-association rule is sufficient for the bounded CO₂–MEA pressure screen.
Cross edges are reciprocal. CO₂ has no self-association energy in the selected
topology; its association is induced through water. The usual combining rules
provide MEA–water values, while the CO₂–water edge uses the retained induced
association volume and half the water association energy.

not present in the topology.

# Limits and evidence type

[]{#numerical-result}

That result is conditional on the tested
association graph, the selected dielectric formulation, the reaction network,
and the available pressure data. It does not establish that the topology is
unique, or that a different association scheme would fail after its own pure
parameter regression.

[]{#conclusion}

Do not place the pair table in
the main input table or treat its derived cross values as independently
regressed parameters. Reopen the topology only with a scheme-specific pure
component comparison and a coupled pressure/speciation assessment.

This is historical formulation and bounded calibration evidence, not independent physical validation.

# Records

This page records the association-formulation decision separately from the
species parameter table. It is an analysis of topology and transfer rules, not
an independently fitted pair-parameter packet. The selected component values
remain in the [overview table](../notebook.qmd#species-parameters).
